messages:
Samira Patel: Need a quick callout on rerank API input shape and launch scope. Customer asks are piling up and we need clear decisions for the next sprint.

Jonah Lee: +1. Brief summary of open decisions please — I can scope impl effort after.

Samira Patel: Top items: 1) candidate payload format (id vs full object) 2) top_k semantics (client-side vs server-side truncation) 3) score normalization across model variants 4) truncation behavior for long passages 5) launch acceptance criteria (perf & accuracy).

Elaine Zhou: For candidate payloads I'd prefer allowing both `id` and inline `item` objects. Many customers already store candidate text externally (id only) while others send full context. Support both, but make id-first the canonical path to keep request sizes small.

Tyler Gomez: Implementation note: supporting both increases parsing complexity. If we do `id` we need a lookup hook (sync vs async). That impacts latency SLO. If we require prefetching on customer side, we keep our runtime simpler.

Samira Patel: Proposal: MVP supports inline `candidates: [{id?: string, text?: string, metadata?: {...}}]`. If `id` is present and `text` is omitted, we return 400 unless `lookup_provider` flag is configured on the endpoint. That keeps safety and avoids hidden async dependencies. Thoughts?

Jonah Lee: Works for product. From infra: add a note that `lookup_provider` must be enabled per-customer and will be rate-limited. Also, it should be opt-in for Dedicated/Private by default.

Elaine Zhou: Agree. Also add a small example in the API docs showing both flows. Example payloads: ```json
{
  "query": "Which article is most relevant?",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c-123"},
    {"text": "Article summary text...", "metadata": {"source": "kb"}}
  ],
  "top_k": 5
}
```

Tyler Gomez: On top_k semantics: do we treat `top_k` as a post-score cutoff (server returns exactly top_k) or as a requested maximum where we may return fewer if results fail filters/truncation? We should be explicit.

Samira Patel: Product preference is: `top_k` = maximum number of candidates to return, but we guarantee we try to populate up to that many. If filtering/truncation removes candidates we return fewer and include `returned_k` and `filtered_reasons` metadata.

Jonah Lee: Ok — that makes client logic easier. We must define `filtered_reasons` enums: `truncated`, `length_exceeded`, `policy_filtered`, `score_threshold`.

Elaine Zhou: Score normalization: customers asked for comparable scores across model variants (e.g., base vs quantized). ML suggestion: return raw model logits and a normalized `score` in [0,1]. Normalization should be per-model calibration map we store per model-version.

Tyler Gomez: Returning logits is risky (data leak + size). I'd prefer returning `raw_score` (float) and `normalized_score`. Keep `raw_score` optional behind a developer flag. Normalized scores should be monotonic and comparable across minor variants.

Samira Patel: Acceptance criteria idea: for launch we require: latency p95 <= 200ms for <=8 candidates inline, cost guidance documented, and score regression < 2% on our evaluation set vs baseline. If `lookup_provider` used, p95 SLO relaxed to 400ms and must be documented.

Jonah Lee: Can we add a canary plan? Rollout: 5% traffic with logging, 25% after 48h if no regressions, then GA. Need to capture eval metrics automatically in Console.

Elaine Zhou: Also add an API param `score_mode` with values `raw`, `normalized`, `both`. Default `normalized`. That gives clients control during migration.

Tyler Gomez: Truncation rules: define token budget per candidate and for total request. Recommend default candidate token limit = 1024, request combined limit = 8192. If a candidate gets truncated we annotate with `truncated: true` and `truncation_strategy: "right"|"left"|"smart"`. Default `smart` = prefer keeping candidate end for relevance in QA.

Samira Patel: Scope negotiation: MVP = inline candidates + optional id-with-lookup (opt-in), `top_k` max return semantics, `normalized_score` default, truncation defaults, `score_mode` param. Defer fancy fallback routing, auto-prefetch, and ML cross-model ensembling to later.

Anna (prod-bot): NOTE: Proposed API contract saved to /product/rerank/proposals/1819003456-v1.yaml (draft).

Jonah Lee: Action items: 1) Elaine to draft API spec + examples (due EOD Thu) 2) Tyler to prototype truncation and request-budget codepath (POC by next Tue) 3) Infra (me) to spec `lookup_provider` rate limits and canary rollout (doc by Fri) 4) Samira to write launch acceptance checklist and customer comms.

Elaine Zhou: I'll include docs for `filtered_reasons` and `score_mode` examples. Also will add sample cURL and SDK snippets.

Samira Patel: Thanks all — let's sync Friday 9:30 for any open tradeoffs. If anyone blocks earlier, drop notes here. :thumbsup:
